license_type: Health Functional Food Product Report (건강기능식품 품목제조신고)
competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS)
pathway_steps: 1. Determine if functional ingredient is on MFDS Recognized Functional Ingredient List or requires new individual recognition
2. For listed ingredients: prepare product specification dossier per MFDS Health Functional Food Code
3. For new ingredients: submit Individual Recognition Application with clinical/scientific evidence
4. Engage MFDS-accredited testing laboratory for product testing per Health Functional Food Code
5. Submit Product Report (품목제조신고서) via MFDS online system
6. Manufacture only at GMP-certified facility (MFDS Health Functional Food GMP)
7. Label must state functional claim exactly as approved by MFDS
8. Import: obtain import report and ensure manufacturer holds overseas GMP equivalent
prerequisites: All ingredients on MFDS approved functional ingredient list
Korean-language label compliant with Health Functional Food Act
typical_timeline_months: 3–12 months (listed ingredients: 3 months; new ingredient recognition: 12–24 months)

gmp_requirements.standard: MFDS Health Functional Food GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice for Health Functional Foods)
gmp_requirements.iso: ISO 22000 considered but MFDS GMP certificate mandatory

renewal_requirements: No fixed renewal; update report if formulation or label changes
reference_regulation: Health Functional Food Act (건강기능식품에 관한 법률); MFDS Health Functional Food Code
notes: South Korea's Health Functional Food (HFF) system is one of Asia's most rigorous. Claims strictly limited to MFDS-approved list. The distinction between HFF (regulated) and general food (unregulated for function) is critical.

pathway_steps: 1. Classify product: Suplemen Kesehatan (Health Supplement) vs Pangan Fungsional (Functional Food) vs Pangan Olahan (Processed Food)
2. Register as foreign manufacturer or appoint local distributor/agent (mandatory for imports)
3. Prepare technical dossier: formulation, CoA, manufacturing evidence, label draft
4. Ensure all ingredients are on BPOM's positive list for health supplements
5. Submit e-registration application via BPOM e-reg portal
6. BPOM review: substantive assessment ~150 business days
7. Respond to BPOM queries within 30 business days
8. Receive Izin Edar number (SD/SP BPOM RI) for label
9. Print Izin Edar number on all labels before distribution
prerequisites: Local distributor/Agent registration in Indonesia (for imports)
All ingredients on BPOM positive list
GMP-certified manufacturing facility (must be auditable by BPOM)

gmp_requirements.standard: CPOTB (Cara Pembuatan Obat Tradisional yang Baik) for traditional; CPKB for cosmetics; GMP equivalent for health supplements
gmp_requirements.overseas: Overseas GMP certificate required; BPOM may conduct factory audit

reference_regulation: BPOM Regulation No. 3 of 2023 (Health Supplements); BPOM Regulation No. 27 of 2022 (Processed Food Labeling)
notes: Indonesia mandates Halal certification via BPJPH (Halal Product Assurance Organising Agency) for food and supplement products. Effective October 2024, halal certification is mandatory for processed foods. This is a significant additional requirement for non-Muslim-majority market entrants.

license_type: Notification of Food (แจ้งรายละเอียดอาหาร) — Health Food / Food Supplement
competent_authority: Thai FDA (Samnakngaan Khanakammakaan Ahan lae Ya — FDA MoPH)
pathway_steps: 1. Classify product under Thai FDA food categories: Controlled food vs Specifically controlled food vs General food
2. Health supplements and vitamins = 'Specifically Controlled Food' requiring notification
3. Ensure all ingredients comply with Thai FDA positive list for food supplements
4. Prepare Thai-language label with compliant claims
5. Submit e-submission via Thai FDA PRIVUS system
6. Receive FDA serial number (เลขสารบบอาหาร) within 7–30 days for compliant submissions
7. Print 13-digit serial number on label
8. Import: customs clearance requires FDA number and import permit
prerequisites: All ingredients on Thai FDA approved list
Thai-language label compliant with Food Act B.E. 2522
fast_track_details: Thai FDA PRIVUS online system enables rapid notification for standard ingredients. Novel ingredients require pre-approval.

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP per Ministerial Notification (food supplement GMP)

renewal_requirements: No fixed renewal; update notification if changes made
reference_regulation: Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979); Thai FDA Ministerial Notification on Food Supplements
notes: Thailand distinguishes functional food from health claims. Health claims are strictly limited to FDA-approved list. Traditional herbal medicines regulated separately under Traditional Medicine Act.

competent_authority: National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA), Ministry of Health Malaysia
pathway_steps: 1. Determine classification: Health Supplement (HS) vs Traditional Medicine (TM) vs Pharmaceutical
2. Health Supplements: notify via QUEST3 portal (online notification system)
3. Ensure ingredients comply with Malaysian Recommended List of Ingredients
4. Prepare label compliant with Health Supplement Order 2019 (HSO 2019)
5. Submit notification — NPRA reviews within 30–90 days
6. Receive notification acknowledgement number (MAL number or Notif. No.)
7. For traditional medicines (Malay, Chinese, Indian): separate registration required
8. Halal certification from JAKIM required for Muslim-targeted products
prerequisites: All ingredients on NPRA approved list
Label in Bahasa Malaysia (or bilingual Bahasa + English)
fast_track_details: Standard notifications for listed ingredients processed within 30 days via QUEST3.

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP for Health Supplements (Malaysian GMP Guidelines)
gmp_requirements.halal: JAKIM Halal certification recommended for majority-Muslim market

renewal_requirements: Renewal 6 months before expiry via QUEST3
reference_regulation: Food Act 1983; Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984; Health Supplement Order 2019
notes: Malaysia has a large traditional medicine sector. Malay, Chinese, and Indian traditional medicines have separate regulatory tracks under the Traditional and Complementary Medicine Act 2016 (Act 775).

license_type: Certificate of Product Registration (CPR) — Food Supplement
pathway_steps: 1. Classify: Food Supplement vs Drug vs Traditional/Herbal (BHDT)
2. Appoint local authorized agent (mandatory for foreign manufacturers)
3. Register manufacturing facility with FDA-PH
4. Prepare dossier: formulation, CoA, safety data, label
5. Submit CPR application via FDA-PH CenterPoint system
6. Substantive review by FDA-PH (typically 3–6 months)
7. Comply with additional requirements or deficiency letters within prescribed time
8. Receive Certificate of Product Registration (CPR)
9. Print CPR number on all labels
prerequisites: All ingredients on FDA-PH approved list
Halal certification if Muslim-targeted (IDCP or other recognized body)

gmp_requirements.standard: FDA-PH GMP requirements; manufacturer must be registered with FDA-PH

reference_regulation: Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009 (RA 9711); FDA Circular No. 2016-005 (Food Supplements)
notes: Philippines FDA distinguishes between food supplements (CPR required), drugs (different pathway), and BHDT (traditional herbal). Label must be in English or Filipino. Claim substantiation is increasingly enforced.

license_type: Self-Declaration (Tự Công Bố) or Announcement of Standard Conformity
competent_authority: Vietnam Food Administration (VFA), Ministry of Health
pathway_steps: 1. Classify product: Thực phẩm chức năng (functional food) is a broad category including supplements, health foods, and fortified foods
2. For standard functional foods with common ingredients: self-declaration (tự công bố) — post declaration online and start selling
3. For functional foods with new ingredients or health claims: submit to Ministry of Health for review
4. Ensure product meets QCVN (National Technical Regulations) applicable to product category
5. Vietnamese-language label mandatory
6. Appointed importer/distributor with Vietnamese business registration required
7. Submit import customs declaration with product dossier
fast_track_details: Self-declaration pathway allows immediate market entry for compliant standard products.

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP per Vietnamese Ministry of Health guidelines

renewal_requirements: Update declaration if formulation or label changes
reference_regulation: Law on Food Safety No. 55/2010/QH12; Decree 15/2018/ND-CP; VFA Circular 43/2014/TT-BYT
notes: Vietnam's self-declaration system is relatively fast for standard products. However, functional food claims are being tightened. Health claims must use Ministry-approved language. Traditional herbal products (thuốc cổ truyền) regulated under separate Drug Law.

license_type: Aviso de Funcionamiento + Health Registration (Registro Sanitario) — Suplemento Alimenticio
competent_authority: COFEPRIS (Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios)
pathway_steps: 1. Determine classification: Suplemento Alimenticio (food supplement) vs Alimento (food) vs Medicamento
2. Obtain Aviso de Funcionamiento (operating notice) for importing company
3. Appoint Responsible Sanitary (profesional con título) — mandatory
4. Prepare Registro Sanitario dossier per NOM-218-SSA1-2011 (Supplements Standard)
5. Submit Registro Sanitario application via COFEPRIS digital window
6. COFEPRIS review: 40–60 working days (by law, often longer in practice)
7. Pay official fee (DAP — derechos de adquisición)
8. Receive Registro Sanitario number (RS-SA-XXXXXX)
9. Print RS number on all Mexican-market labels
prerequisites: Aviso de Funcionamiento for Mexican company
All ingredients comply with NOM-218-SSA1-2011 permitted list

gmp_requirements.standard: NOM-251-SSA1-2009 Good Manufacturing Practices for Food
gmp_requirements.overseas: Foreign GMP equivalent required; COFEPRIS may inspect

reference_regulation: Ley General de Salud; NOM-218-SSA1-2011 (Suplementos Alimenticios); NOM-051-SCFI/SSA1-2010 (Labeling)
notes: Mexico's NOM-051 food labeling standard was revised in 2020 to include front-of-pack black octagonal warning seals for excess sugar, sodium, saturated fat, trans fat, and calories. This is mandatory for all food and supplement products.

license_type: Registro Nacional de Producto Alimenticio (RNPA) — Suplemento Dietario
competent_authority: ANMAT (Administración Nacional de Medicamentos, Alimentos y Tecnología Médica)
pathway_steps: 1. Classify as Suplemento Dietario under Código Alimentario Argentino (CAA) Chapter XX
2. Appoint Argentine importer/representative with Habilitación ANMAT
3. Ensure all ingredients comply with CAA Chapter XX positive list
4. Register with provincial health authority (for manufacturing) or ANMAT (for imports)
5. Submit RNPA (Registro Nacional de Producto Alimenticio) application
6. ANMAT review: typically 180+ working days
7. Receive RNPA number
8. Label in Spanish (Argentine format) with RNPA number

gmp_requirements.standard: CAA GMP (Buenas Prácticas de Fabricación) equivalent to Codex Alimentarius GMP

reference_regulation: Código Alimentario Argentino (CAA) Chapter XX; Resolución ANMAT 1637/2015 (Suplementos Dietarios); MERCOSUR GMC Res. 58/10
notes: Argentina is part of MERCOSUR. For Suplementos Dietarios, ANMAT is the primary regulator. Front-of-pack nutritional warnings (sellos) are under development following Chilean model.

license_type: Registro Sanitario / Permiso Sanitario — Suplemento Dietario
competent_authority: INVIMA (Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos)
pathway_steps: 1. Classify as Suplemento Dietario under Decreto 3249 de 2006
2. Appoint Colombian importer/representative
3. Verify all ingredients comply with permitted ingredient list
4. Submit Registro Sanitario application to INVIMA online system
5. INVIMA review: 30–60 working days (legally); practice often longer
6. Receive Registro Sanitario INVIMA number
7. Label in Spanish (Colombian format) with RS number
8. Annual sanitary permit renewal

gmp_requirements.standard: BPM (Buenas Prácticas de Manufactura) as per Colombian regulations

reference_regulation: Decreto 3249 de 2006 (Suplementos Dietarios); Resolución 288 de 2008 (Nutritional Labeling); Resolución 333 de 2011
notes: Colombia adopted nutritional warning labels (octagonal) in 2021 via Resolución 810 de 2021. Products high in sodium, sugar, saturated fat, or trans fat must carry front-of-pack warning seals.

license_type: Product Registration — Emirates Conformity Assessment (ECAS) + DHA/DOH Notification
competent_authority: ESMA (Emirates Authority for Standardization and Metrology) + Emirate Health Authorities
pathway_steps: 1. Verify product complies with applicable UAE.S (Emirates Standard) — food categories mapped to UAE.S/GSO standards
2. Obtain Halal certification from UAE-recognized body (mandatory for meat, poultry; recommended for all food)
3. Register with Dubai Municipality (for Dubai), Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA for Abu Dhabi), or Sharjah/other emirate authorities
4. Apply for Emirates Conformity Assessment (if product category requires ECAS mark)
5. Import: Dubai Municipality food registration via eServices portal
6. Ensure Arabic-language label (mandatory) plus English
7. All labels must include: production date, expiry date, country of origin, ingredients in Arabic
documents_required: Import permit from relevant emirate authority
fast_track_details: Dubai Municipality offers expedited review for products from GCC countries. GCC mutual recognition applies.

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP per UAE.S 14159 (Food Safety — Hygiene Requirements) and ISO 22000

renewal_requirements: Annual renewal with each emirate authority
post_approval_obligations: Comply with UAE Ministry of Health recall procedures
reference_regulation: UAE Food Safety Law No. 10 of 2015; UAE.S GSO standards; Dubai Municipality Food Safety Department regulations
notes: UAE food regulation is complex due to the federal/emirate dual system. Dubai and Abu Dhabi have different portals and requirements. Halal certification is practically mandatory for market access — non-Halal products must be clearly marked and can only be sold in specific outlets.

license_type: Product Registration — SFDA Health Supplement Registration
pathway_steps: 1. Appoint Saudi licensed agent/importer (mandatory)
2. Verify all ingredients on SFDA Positive List for health supplements
3. Obtain Halal certification from recognized Saudi Halal body (SASO-accredited CB)
4. Prepare registration dossier per SFDA Guidance
5. Submit via SFDA GHAD (General Administration of Health Food and Supplements) portal
6. SFDA review: 90–180 days
7. Receive SFDA registration number
8. Arabic label mandatory with SFDA registration number
9. Import: customs clearance via SFDA Trusted Trader Program

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP equivalent (SFDA evaluates overseas GMP certificates)

reference_regulation: SFDA Resolution on Dietary Supplements; SFDA Food and Drug General Law
notes: Saudi Arabia is the largest GCC market. SFDA is one of the most stringent regulators in the region. GCC product registration mutual recognition (if product registered in another GCC country) may accelerate review. Banned substances list extensive.

competent_authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry — General Directorate of Food and Control (BSGM)
pathway_steps: 1. Classify as Gıda Takviyesi (food supplement) per Turkish Food Supplements Regulation 2013
2. Ensure all ingredients on Turkish permitted list (aligned with EU Directive 2002/46/EC for vitamins/minerals)
3. Appoint Turkish importer registered with Ministry of Agriculture
4. Submit Gıda Takviyesi notification via SOGUT portal
5. Ministry review: typically 30–60 days
6. Receive notification number
7. Turkish-language label mandatory with notification number
8. Halal label permitted but not mandatory (Turkey is secular but majority Muslim)

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP per Turkish Food Codex (Türk Gıda Kodeksi) — aligned with EU GMP

post_approval_obligations: Annual compliance with Turkish Food Codex
reference_regulation: Gıda Takviyeleri Yönetmeliği (Food Supplements Regulation) 2013; Turkish Food Codex Regulation
notes: Turkey aligns food supplement regulation largely with EU law due to its customs union status. However, Turkey is not an EU member and national notification is required separately from EU. Turkish labels must be in Turkish.

competent_authority: Ministry of Health Israel — Food Control Services
pathway_steps: 1. Verify product complies with Israeli dietary supplement regulations under Public Health Regulations (Food) 1983
2. Check if product falls under restricted list requiring prior approval
3. Register importer with Israeli Ministry of Health
4. Obtain import permit for first shipment
5. Ensure label in Hebrew (mandatory) plus English or other
6. Products from recognized regulatory authorities (FDA, EU, TGA) receive faster review
7. Novel ingredients require pre-approval from Ministry of Health
fast_track_details: Products from FDA/EU/TGA approved manufacturers receive expedited review.
reference_regulation: Public Health Regulations (Food) 1983 (as amended); Dietary Supplements Regulations 2009
notes: Israel follows a relatively permissive dietary supplement framework. Products from FDA/EU/TGA jurisdictions are generally accepted with streamlined review. Kosher certification is commercially important but not legally mandatory.

license_type: Registration — Complementary Medicine (Section 14 of Medicines Act)
competent_authority: SAHPRA (South African Health Products Regulatory Authority)
pathway_steps: 1. Classify as Complementary Medicine (vitamins, minerals, herbals, homeopathics, etc.) under Medicines Act 101/1965
2. Check SAHPRA General Safety and Complementary Medicines Registration Framework
3. Determine registration category: Category A (low risk, self-registration) or Category B/C (higher evidence requirements)
4. Prepare dossier per SAHPRA Common Technical Document (CTD) for complementary medicines
5. Submit registration application via SAHPRA online portal
6. SAHPRA review: significantly backlogged — 2–5 years in practice
7. Receive registration certificate
8. Label must include registration number
prerequisites: South African responsible person / local manufacturer

gmp_requirements.standard: Good Manufacturing Practice per WHO Technical Report 961/2011 (Annex 3)

reference_regulation: Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965; SAHPRA Complementary Medicines Registration Framework
notes: SAHPRA is severely backlogged with complementary medicine registrations. Many products currently on the market are under 'grace period' enforcement discretion while awaiting registration. Practical market entry is possible but regulatory status is technically unregistered pending SAHPRA review.

license_type: Product Registration — NAFDAC Certificate of Registration
competent_authority: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control)
pathway_steps: 1. Appoint Nigerian registered importer/agent
2. Classify product: food supplement vs herbal medicine vs food
3. Prepare dossier: formulation, CoA, safety data, label
4. Submit NAFDAC e-registration application
5. NAFDAC Coordinating Director review: 3–6 months
6. Product screening and laboratory testing by NAFDAC (mandatory sample submission)
7. Site inspection of manufacturer (for domestic; overseas inspection for imports)
8. Receive NAFDAC Registration Number (NAFDAC REG. NO.)
9. Print NAFDAC number on all labels

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP per WHO standards (NAFDAC enforces WHO GMP)
gmp_requirements.inspection: NAFDAC may conduct overseas factory inspection for new applicants

reference_regulation: NAFDAC Act Cap N1 LFN 2004; NAFDAC Regulations for Food and Drug Registration
notes: NAFDAC is the gateway to the entire West African market. Nigeria is Africa's largest economy. NAFDAC's mandatory laboratory testing and frequent factory inspections add time and cost. Products found substandard face immediate recall and criminal prosecution. NAFDAC is actively combating counterfeits.

license_type: Product Listing — PPB (Pharmacy and Poisons Board) for Health Supplements
pathway_steps: 1. Classify as health supplement under Kenya Pharmacy and Poisons Act Cap 244
2. Appoint Kenyan licensed pharmaceutical agent
3. Prepare dossier per PPB registration guidelines
4. Submit registration application via PPB online portal
5. PPB review and evaluation
6. Pay required fees
7. Receive PPB registration/listing number
8. Label in English (Kenya's official language) with PPB number

gmp_requirements.standard: WHO GMP standards enforced by PPB

reference_regulation: Pharmacy and Poisons Act Cap 244; PPB Guidelines for Health Supplements
notes: Kenya is East Africa's largest pharmaceutical market and a hub for regional distribution. PPB registration is mandatory for health supplements. EAC (East African Community) harmonisation is underway, which may eventually allow mutual recognition across Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, and Burundi.

license_type: Notification to Cantonal Authority (Kantonschemiker) — Food Supplement
competent_authority: FSVO (Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office) + Cantonal Chemists
pathway_steps: 1. Verify product complies with Swiss Foodstuffs Act (LMG/LDA) and Food and Utility Articles Ordinance (LGV/ODAlOUs)
2. Verify Swiss specific requirements for food supplements (aligned with EU but with Swiss-specific limits)
3. Notify local cantonal authority (Kantonschemiker) of the canton where first sold — informal notification
4. Ensure label complies with Swiss Food Labelling Ordinance (LKV/OEDAl)
5. German, French, and Italian label required (all three national languages for national distribution)
6. No pre-market approval needed for standard supplements with permitted ingredients
prerequisites: Labels in German, French, and Italian
fast_track_details: Switzerland has no pre-market approval for standard food supplements — instant market access if compliant.

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP per Swiss GMP Guidelines (V-CH-GMP / ICH Q10 equivalent)

reference_regulation: Lebensmittelgesetz (LMG) 2017; Lebensmittel- und Gebrauchsgegenständeverordnung (LGV); Swiss Dietary Supplement Ordinance
notes: Switzerland broadly follows EU food law but has its own national legislation. A product legal in the EU is generally legal in Switzerland but Swiss-specific label requirements (trilingual) apply. SWISSMEDIC regulates therapeutic products (medicinal claims trigger drug regulation).
